title: Strawberries & Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Vanilla cupcakes with real strawberry compote folded in, topped with whipped cream cheese frosting, ready in about 45 minutes.
description: These cupcakes taste like strawberry shortcake in cupcake form. I cook down fresh strawberries into a thick compote and fold it right into the batter, so every bite has real fruit flavor. No food coloring here, just ripe berries doing the work. The frosting is whipped cream cheese, lighter than a basic buttercream but still holds its swirl. I tested this recipe three times in my own kitchen to get the compote thick enough that it does not sink to the bottom. This is a great spring or summer bake when strawberries are at their best. It also works with frozen berries in a pinch, just drain them well after cooking. Serve these at a birthday party or a weekend brunch. They travel well if you keep them chilled until an hour before serving.
instructions: Cook chopped strawberries, 3 tablespoons sugar, and lemon juice in a small pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and jammy.
Cool the compote fully in the fridge for at least 20 minutes before using.
Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin pan with 12 liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl.
Beat butter and sugar together for 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with milk, mixing just until combined.
Fold in 1/2 cup of the cooled strawberry compote by hand, leaving small streaks of fruit.
Divide batter into liners, filling each two thirds full, and bake 16 to 18 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes fully on a wire rack before frosting.
Beat cold cream cheese until smooth, then add powdered sugar and beat again.
In a separate bowl, whip cold heavy cream to stiff peaks, then fold into the cream cheese mix.
Pipe the frosting onto cooled cupcakes and top with sliced strawberries.
tips: Cool the compote completely before folding it in, or it will melt the butter in your batter.
Use cold cream cheese and cold heavy cream for a frosting that holds its shape.
If using frozen strawberries, thaw and drain them well before cooking the compote.
Frost cupcakes within a few hours of serving since the whipped frosting is softer than regular buttercream.

faq.question: Why is my strawberry compote sinking to the bottom of the cupcake?
faq.answer: The compote is likely too thin or still warm when folded in. Cook it until thick and jammy, then chill it fully before adding it to the batter.

faq.question: Can I use strawberry jam instead of making compote?
faq.answer: You can, but choose a low sugar jam and reduce the added sugar in the compote step. Homemade compote gives a fresher, less sweet result.

faq.question: Will the whipped cream cheese frosting hold up at a party?
faq.answer: It holds fine at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours. For longer events, keep cupcakes chilled and bring them out closer to serving time.

faq.question: Can I make this recipe with frozen strawberries?
faq.answer: Yes, thaw them first and drain the extra liquid before cooking the compote, so it does not turn out too watery.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring real strawberry flavor without any artificial color or flavoring. Keep the compote cold, whip the frosting well, and you have a classic bake that tastes like summer.
